name: Post-Employment Non-Compete Restriction
description: Covenant prohibiting employment with competitors following separation from employment.
patterns: shall not (?:join|work with|be employed by).*competitor.*(?:after termination|after leaving|for a period of)
legalSource: Indian Contract Act, 1872 - Section 27 (Agreement in restraint of trade is void ab initio; Percept D'Mark v. Zaheer Khan, 2006 SC)
explanation: Any covenant restraining an individual from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business after termination of employment is void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act.
caveat: Non-compete covenants during active employment are legally enforceable; restraints extending beyond termination are void under Indian jurisprudence.

name: Disproportionate Employment Bond Penalty
description: Liquidated damages penalty in employment service bond exceeding actual demonstrable training expenses.
legalSource: Indian Contract Act, 1872 - Section 74 & Article 23 of the Constitution of India (Prohibition of bonded labor)
explanation: Service bonds stipulating exorbitant damages unrelated to actual documented training expenses act as an illegal penalty rather than legitimate compensation.
caveat: Employers may recover actual, verifiable specialized training costs amortized across completed months of service.

name: Excessive Notice Period Exceeding 90 Days
description: Unreasonably long mandatory notice period without buyout or early-release mechanisms.
patterns: notice period.*(?:exceeding 3 months|4 months|6 months|180 days)
legalSource: Industrial Disputes Act, 1847 & Model Standing Orders on Employment Terms
explanation: Excessive notice periods without standard pay-in-lieu options restrict employee career mobility and may be considered an indirect restraint of trade.
caveat: Key management personnel and specialized researchers may legitimately require longer transition windows than standard employees.

name: Standard Mutual Notice with Salary in Lieu
description: Standard mutual notice of 30 days or salary in lieu thereof.
patterns: (?:either party|both parties).*(?:terminate|end employment).*(?:one month|30 days).*notice.*salary in lieu
one month written notice or payment of salary in lieu
legalSource: Standard Industrial Employment Norms & Indian Contract Act Principles of Mutuality
explanation: A reciprocal notice clause allowing termination with 30 days notice or basic salary in lieu adheres to standard fair employment benchmarks.
caveat: Statutory notice during probationary periods is typically shorter (e.g. 15 days).
